analysis: The only changed file is docs/developer/test.md. The patch adds a documentation block at head lines 551-561 describing a `LocalTokenizerByteFallbackTests` command (`swift test --skip-build --filter ...`) that checks Gemma 4 byte-fallback tokens (`<0xHH>`) in the local tokenizer decode path. No source code, protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache or fan-helper behavior changes. The supplied base text units (lines 1843-2535) are unchanged surrounding documentation; they describe CPU-only test procedures and hardware qualification gates, and that content sits outside the changed hunk. I checked them against T-041 (prefix cache). The text on tenant partitioning and SSD record encoding is descriptive and does not alter the documented cache posture: HMAC-keyed names, a 30-minute TTL and tenant-scoped salts. No new attack surface, no weakened assumption, and no need to update the threat model. The new test doc is about tokenizer decode correctness, which has no direct link to A-001 confidentiality. The tests it describes are not evidence of a regression. Remaining uncertainty: the actual tokenizer code and test source are not supplied, so this pass cannot judge their security behavior. Only the documentation was reviewed.
